issue.title: Separate create-refusal text from when_to_use for non-agent-creatable types
issue.description:
`resolve_created_task_type()` in `src/sase/task_types/fields.py` appends the type's `when_to_use` after "cannot be created by agents" when `agent_creatable` is false.

That reads as a contradiction for a type whose `when_to_use` is an invitation (the builtin `feature` type: "File one when you discovered a product or capability idea..."). `flag` avoids the contradiction only because its `when_to_use` is deliberately written as the refusal explanation.

Discovered while implementing the approved plan `sase/repos/plans/202608/feature_task_type_scoping.md`, which suppresses `feature` with `agent_creatable: false` for every non-sase project. An agent that ignored its instruction note and ran `sase bead create -T task(feature)` would then see the invitation text after the refusal.

Out of scope for that plan: improving the message means giving the spec a separate refusal field, which is a larger schema-and-wording change.

task_type_fields.proposal: Give a task-type spec an optional refusal field (separate from `when_to_use`) and have `resolve_created_task_type()` print that text after "cannot be created by agents". Keep `flag`'s current when_to_use-as-refusal behavior as the fallback so existing types do not break.
task_type_fields.why_out_of_scope: The approved feature-scoping plan only disables creating `feature` beads outside the sase project. Changing the create-refusal message needs a new spec key, Rust validator/digest work, and wording for every type whose when_to_use is an invitation rather than a refusal.
